subject.title: feat: add lease-bound metadata to session spawns

question: Should OpenClaw core own this external Agentic OS lease-and-metadata protocol, or should core expose only a generic host-authorization seam for an owner plugin or downstream adapter to implement the protocol?
rationale: This choice determines a long-lived public Gateway and persistence contract; it cannot be resolved safely as a mechanical review repair without maintainer intent about core scope and API ownership.

options.title: Use a generic core seam
options.body: Keep only reusable spawn authorization and lifecycle hooks in core, then move Agentic OS-specific methods, metadata, and replay semantics to the owner integration.

options.title: Sponsor the core protocol
options.body: Accept the new public core API only after explicitly owning its compatibility, documentation, restart recovery, and release-contract obligations.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Close or defer the branch if no maintainer wants to support this external orchestration contract as a maintained product surface.

recommendation.title: Use a generic core seam
recommendation.body: Keep only reusable spawn authorization and lifecycle hooks in core, then move Agentic OS-specific methods, metadata, and replay semantics to the owner integration.

likelyOwner.reason: yuzuqiang is the only evidence-backed proposer for the external contract and can clarify the intended owner boundary, while final product acceptance remains a repository maintainer decision.
